findings.title: Plain Error thrown instead of TRPCError; delegation credentials not handled
findings.body: A plain `Error` becomes an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) in tRPC, so a not-found or unauthorized credential is reported as a server failure and shows up in error monitoring. It should throw `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` or `FORBIDDEN`. The ownership check also only matches credentials in the DB with `userId`. Delegation credentials are in-memory with negative ids and the UI passes them through, so deleting their cache will always fail.

findings.title: deleteCache success does not refresh connectedCalendars query
findings.body: After deleting cache, the mutation only calls `onSuccess?.()`, which is an optional prop. The disconnect mutation invalidates `connectedCalendars`, but deleteCacheMutation does not. If `onChanged` is not provided, or does not refetch, the "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option stay visible after the cache is gone, which contradicts the expected UI update. It needs `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in onSuccess/onSettled.

findings.title: updateMany with empty data does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object. Prisma `updateMany` does not apply `@updatedAt` when no fields change, so this is likely a no-op while still costing a DB round trip. The comment claims it updates `updatedAt`, but it does not do so reliably. The PR notes also say the frontend does not use this value, so the call looks like dead or misleading code that adds a write on every cache refresh/webhook.

findings.title: Cache timestamp semantics are misleading and the mock is missing from the connected-calendars path
findings.body: `updatedAt` is `@default(now()) @updatedAt`, and the migration backfills existing rows with `NOW()` at migration time. All pre-existing cache rows therefore show a "last updated" of the deploy time, not their real update time. In `connectedCalendarsHandler`, `new CalendarCacheRepository()` is used directly rather than the `CalendarCache.init` factory that returns the mock when calendar-cache is disabled. Cache status is therefore queried and displayed even when the feature is disabled, and the mock's `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is never used.

findings.title: Hardcoded en-US date formatting ignores user locale
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see US-style dates. It should use the user's locale (e.g. `i18n.language`). Also `hasCache` is typed as `Date | null | false | undefined`, and `cacheUpdatedAt` is serialized over tRPC (superjson) as a Date, so this works only because of superjson.

findings.title: Extra DB query on every connectedCalendars call
findings.body: Every call to `connectedCalendars`, which is also used in onboarding and event-type settings, now runs an additional `groupBy` on CalendarCache even for non-Google credentials, and negative (in-memory delegation) credential ids are included in the `IN` list. Filter to Google Calendar DB credentials (`credentialId > 0`) before querying.

findings.title: macOS-only sed and unrelated dev script included in feature PR
findings.body: `sed -i ''` works only on BSD/macOS sed and breaks on GNU/Linux, where `''` is interpreted as the script and the real script as a filename. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the cwd, so the script writes to a different path depending on where it is run. The script is unrelated to the cache feature and also hardcodes /tmp paths. The unrelated `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` is likewise out of scope.
